overview: CyberAgent is a Japanese internet company founded in 1998 and listed on the TSE Prime Market, operating across three core businesses: Internet Advertisement (ad agency/DSP and AI-driven ad services), Media & IP (centered on the ABEMA streaming platform, WINTICKET betting-information service, and anime/IP production), and Games (led by subsidiary Cygames and its hit mobile titles). The company also runs a small corporate-venture-capital Investment Development segment. Operations are concentrated in Japan with growing overseas game sales; fiscal year ends September 30.

business_model.summary: Revenue is a mix of agency/programmatic internet advertising fees (largest and most stable segment), subscription plus advertising revenue from the ABEMA streaming and IP business (now profitable after a decade of investment losses), and high-margin mobile/console game sales (the main profit engine, with recurring live-service monetization via gacha/in-app purchases). FY2025 marked the 28th consecutive year of revenue growth.
business_model.customer_type: Mixed: B2B (advertisers/agencies for the Ad segment) and B2C (ABEMA viewers/subscribers, game players)
business_model.geographic_mix: Predominantly Japan; Games segment has meaningful and growing overseas sales from global hit titles; Advertisement and Media businesses are almost entirely domestic

main_competitors: Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, U-NEXT, TVer (streaming)
Bandai Namco, Mixi, DeNA, Sega, Konami, Colopl (mobile games)
competitive_position.market_position: Leading independent Japanese digital ad agency/AI-ad player; ABEMA is Japan's largest homegrown free ad-supported streaming (FAST) platform but trails Netflix and Amazon Prime Video in paid SVOD share; Cygames is one of Japan's top-tier mobile game studios (Uma Musume, Shadowverse, Granblue Fantasy, Princess Connect) with occasional global hits

moat_factors.description: Owned game IP (Uma Musume, Granblue Fantasy, Shadowverse) and growing anime production create multi-layered monetization (games, streaming, merchandising) feeding back into ABEMA content

moat_factors.factor: Scale in Japanese digital ad buying
moat_factors.description: Long-standing agency relationships and proprietary AI/programmatic tools support share in a market still shifting from traditional to digital media

ABEMA built an 10-year content/brand lead domestically in free ad-supported live TV plus sports/variety rights (e.g., boxing, elections, anime simulcasts) that is costly for a new entrant to replicate
Deep relationships with Japanese talent agencies, broadcasters (co-owner TV Asahi) and content producers support exclusive programming

weaknesses: ABEMA/Media & IP only just returned to profitability in FY2025 after roughly a decade of losses; durability of margins is unproven
Heavy reliance on a small number of game hit titles and an aging core IP portfolio (Granblue Fantasy, Shadowverse) for segment profit
Internet Advertisement segment lost major clients in H2 FY2025 and faces margin pressure from AI-related investment spend
Minority-interest drag: Cygames' non-controlling interest materially reduces net income attributable to parent
Smaller content budget than Netflix/Amazon for premium drama/film, limiting ABEMA's ability to compete head-on in paid SVOD

growth_drivers: ABEMA/Media & IP segment scaling multi-layered revenue (advertising, subscription (ABEMA Premium), PPV, merchandising) now that it is profitable
Anime & IP Division and multimedia franchise strategy leveraging owned game IP into anime, merchandise and licensing
Continued global expansion of game titles (casual and major flagship titles) driving Game segment sales and profit growth (+37.8% YoY sales in 9M FY2026)
AI Division investment in the Internet Advertisement business, aiming to capture new AI-driven ad products and tools even though near-term it is a cost drag
WINTICKET (public bicycle/boat racing betting information) as an ancillary high-growth media property
Secular shift of Japanese ad budgets from traditional (TV/print) to digital media, a multi-year tailwind for the core Ad segment
Management succession to new President Takahiro Yamauchi (effective Dec 2025) intended to set a fresh medium/long-term growth strategy by 2027-2029

business.description: Company disclosed losing some major advertising clients in H2 FY2025, pressuring segment profit even as sales grew

Game segment profit is driven by a handful of flagship titles (Uma Musume, Granblue Fantasy, Shadowverse, casual titles); any decline in engagement or failure of new launches would hit consolidated profit materially given the segment's outsized profit contribution
ABEMA competes against much larger-budget global SVOD players (Netflix, Amazon) and domestic rivals (U-NEXT, TVer) for both viewers and ad dollars

The CyberOwl matter (see regulatory risks) revealed inadequate segregation of duties at a subsidiary; risk that similar issues could recur elsewhere in CyberAgent's large, decentralized subsidiary structure

financial.description: Cygames minority interest reduces the portion of game-segment profit attributable to parent shareholders

Outstanding convertible-bond-type bonds with share acquisition rights (~¥40bn) and bank borrowings create modest refinancing/dilution risk, though net cash position remains positive (~¥113bn at Jun 2026)
Management explicitly flags the Game business's inherent volatility when giving wide full-year guidance ranges (e.g., FY2026 operating income range initially ¥50-60bn)

regulatory.description: An internal investigation (initiated March 2025, report received April 16, 2025) found that a CyberOwl director in a dual business/management-control role had altered affiliate-advertising performance-fee accrual coefficients since 2020, overstating CyberOwl's standalone sales. Estimated sales overstatements were approximately JPY 40m (FY2020), JPY 311m (FY2021), JPY 763m (FY2022), JPY 855m (FY2023) and JPY 1,759m (FY2024) — roughly JPY 3.7bn cumulative at the subsidiary level, immaterial to CyberAgent's consolidated results. CyberAgent filed amended annual securities reports (Yuho) and quarterly corrections covering FY2021-FY2025 periods on/around May 15, 2025, dismissed the responsible executive, cut CEO Fujita's pay 30% and the CyberOwl president's pay 10% for three months, and announced remedial controls (revenue recognized only on advertiser-approved amounts, new fraud-detection tooling, and separation of business/management-control roles). Company stated the consolidated impact was minor and did not change forecasts; stock reportedly rebounded once the matter was resolved.

ABEMA operates adjacent to broadcasting law and advertising standards in Japan; increased platform regulation (e.g., child safety, gambling-adjacent content for WINTICKET) is a modest ongoing compliance risk
Japanese and overseas regulatory scrutiny of gacha-style monetization in mobile games is a long-running industry-wide risk for the Games segment

macro.description: Internet Advertisement revenue is tied to corporate ad budgets, which are sensitive to Japanese and global economic conditions
Weak yen raises costs for licensed overseas content and global game development/marketing, though it also aids overseas game sales translated back to yen
Analysts flag rising content procurement costs for ABEMA (sports rights, originals) as a margin risk even after reaching profitability

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Japan's digital advertising market continues to grow and take share from traditional media; mobile/online gaming in Japan remains large with periodic blockbuster hits and growing overseas monetization; domestic SVOD/FAST streaming market is growing but concentrated among a few global and large domestic platforms
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - ad revenue is cyclical with corporate spending; game revenue is driven by hit-title cycles and live-service engagement; media/streaming has a structural (non-cyclical) subscriber/engagement growth component
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct exposure; net cash position (~¥113bn) limits financing cost risk; convertible bond carries modest dilution risk if converted
key_input_costs: Content/programming rights (sports, anime, originals) for ABEMA
Game development and marketing/UA (user acquisition) spend
Personnel costs (headcount ~8,900 and rising with new graduate hiring)

recent_developments.event: FY2025 full-year results: net sales ¥874.0bn (+9.1% YoY, 28th consecutive year of growth), operating income ¥71.7bn (+78.9%), net income ¥31.7bn (+98.2%); Media & IP business returned to operating profit for the first time in 10 years; FY2026 initial guidance set at sales ¥880bn, operating income ¥50-60bn

Leadership succession: Takahiro Yamauchi became Representative Director and President effective December 12, 2025, the first change in CyberAgent's presidency in 27 years; founder Susumu Fujita moved to Representative Director and Chairman, remaining the largest shareholder

CyberOwl subsidiary accounting matter concluded: internal investigation report received, amended securities reports (Yuho) and quarterly corrections filed for FY2021-FY2025 periods (May 15, 2025), responsible executive dismissed, temporary pay cuts for CEO/CyberOwl president, remedial controls announced; company stated consolidated impact was minor
H1 FY2026 (six months to March 2026) results: operating income up ~79% YoY to a record ¥52.4bn; ABEMA posted a ¥10.3bn profit; management called full-year guidance achievement 'certain'

Q3 FY2026 (nine months to June 2026) results: net sales ¥709.3bn (+12.2% YoY), operating income ¥67.4bn (+38.2% YoY), net income ¥36.0bn (+49.5% YoY); Game segment sales +37.8% YoY on strong flagship and casual titles; FY2026 full-year guidance raised to sales ¥950.0bn (+8.7% YoY) and operating income ¥77.0bn (+7.4% YoY); year-end dividend forecast raised to ¥20/share (from ¥19)

Analyst sentiment stayed constructive: consensus largely Buy-rated with price targets broadly ¥1,500-¥2,500 (e.g., Macquarie ¥2,000, UBS ¥2,500, JPMorgan ¥1,800); commentary flagged rising content costs and streaming competition as the main watch items even as ABEMA and Games continued to outperform

items.notes: Raised from original ¥880.0bn guidance (Nov 2025); implies +8.7% YoY vs FY2025's ¥874.0bn
Raised from original ¥50-60bn range; implies +7.4% YoY vs FY2025's ¥71.7bn, driven by strong Media & IP, Advertisement and Game results

items.metric: Net income attributable to owners of the parent
items.notes: +29.5% YoY vs FY2025's ¥31.7bn; basic EPS guidance ¥80.85
Raised from ¥19.00 forecast given at FY2025 results; targets DOE of 5%+ policy established FY2017

guidance.management_commentary: New President Takahiro Yamauchi characterized Q3 results as 'better than we expected internally,' citing strong ABEMA and Game segment profit growth. At H1 FY2026, management described achievement of full-year guidance as 'a certain situation.' Guidance acknowledges the Game business's inherent earnings volatility; the company does not expect further financial impact from the FY2021-FY2025 CyberOwl accounting corrections.

bull_case: ABEMA/Media & IP business has reached sustained profitability after a decade of investment losses, unlocking a large (previously loss-making) revenue base as a profit contributor
Game segment is firing on multiple cylinders with both flagship titles and new casual-game hits, delivering +37.8% YoY sales and +44.8% YoY operating income in 9M FY2026
28 consecutive years of revenue growth and a net cash balance sheet (~¥113bn) provide resilience and capital-return capacity (dividend raised twice within FY2026)
Structural tailwind from the ongoing shift of Japanese advertising budgets from traditional media to digital/internet, benefiting the largest segment

Multimedia franchise/IP strategy (games -> anime -> ABEMA -> merchandising) creates multiple monetization layers from owned IP, with new leadership (Yamauchi) tasked with articulating the next phase of strategy
bear_case: Media & IP profitability is nascent (first profitable year in a decade) and unproven through a full content-investment or competitive cycle; rising sports/content rights costs could compress newly-won margins

Game segment profit is concentrated in a handful of aging flagship titles; a slowdown in Uma Musume, Granblue Fantasy or Shadowverse engagement, or failure of new launches, would disproportionately hit consolidated operating income
Internet Advertisement segment already lost major clients in H2 FY2025 and is absorbing AI-related investment costs, pressuring the largest segment's profitability even as sales grow

The CyberOwl subsidiary accounting matter, while deemed immaterial at the consolidated level, exposed weak internal controls (dual business/management-control roles) in a large, decentralized subsidiary structure, raising governance questions about other subsidiaries
ABEMA remains a distant player in paid SVOD behind Netflix and Amazon Prime Video in Japan, limiting the segment's ceiling versus globally-scaled competitors with far larger content budgets
Leadership transition risk: first CEO change in 27 years (Dec 2025) introduces execution/strategy uncertainty during a multi-year (2027-2029) handover period
